title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 27
paragraphs: And heaven, it seems, tends to give signs beforehand whenever great evils are about to fall on a city or a race of men; for to the Chians too, before these events, remarkable signs had come. In the first place, when they had sent a chorus of a hundred young men to Delphi, only two returned home, the remaining ninety-eight having been seized by a plague and carried off. And secondly, in their city at about the same time—just before the sea-fight—as some children were being taught in school, the roof fell in on them, so that of a hundred and twenty children only one escaped. These signs the god showed to them beforehand; and after this the sea-fight came upon them and brought their state to its knees; and since the Chians had suffered great loss, Histiaeus without difficulty effected the conquest of them.
